CONTENT: Name the repository in kebab-case with clear purpose and audience keywords
DESCRIPTION: Choose a concise repository name using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. Include terms that state the project purpose and primary audience so the name is easy to scan in GitHub lists and easier to find via keyword search. Avoid vague or internal-only wording unless it is a recognised team standard.

CONTENT: Write a concise repository description with purpose, audience, and keywords
DESCRIPTION: Write a single sentence that explains what the repository does, who it helps, and the main value it provides. Use plain language and include one or two words people are likely to search for so it is easier to find in GitHub search and quicker to understand in lists and profile views.

CONTENT: Set repository visibility intentionally (Public or Private)
DESCRIPTION: Choose visibility before first push and confirm it matches your collaboration and security needs. CONTENT: Pin this repo to your GitHub profile (active or priority projects only)
DESCRIPTION: If this repo is active or strategically important, add it to your pinned repositories so visitors can quickly find it and understand your current focus.

CONTENT: Set GitHub repository watch level intentionally (Not watching, Releases only, Watching, or Ignoring)
DESCRIPTION: In the repository Watch menu, pick the lowest level that fits your role. Use Not watching to reduce noise, Releases only to follow releases without issue/PR noise, Watching (all activity) for active maintainers, and Ignoring to mute notifications. Review after 2 weeks and adjust if you miss important updates or get too many notifications.
